subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Great to hear about the ingestion volume you mentioned and the realtime scoring use case — appreciate the context.

Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:
- Goal: validate Hosted API for an initial evaluation (integration, latency, and cost profile) before deciding whether to move to Dedicated capacity for production.
- What we’ll provide: a short evaluation plan, a temporary eval API key, and a quickstart guide to get your engineers running against our Hosted endpoints.
- What you’ll do: run the test harness (sample requests + 10k tokens/day for 7 days), share latency samples and any quality regressions, and let us know estimated production QPS.

Hosted API notes (short):
- Endpoints: POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate (text gen), POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings
- Streaming: SSE supported; SDKs provide streaming helpers
- Default trial rate limits: 60 requests/minute (burst to 120) and 600k tokens/day. We can temporarily raise the RPS for the evaluation window — let me know the peak QPS you expect.
- Pricing: usage-based per-token (we’ll apply eval credits for the trial).

I attached a short quickstart (redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf) and will follow up shortly with the eval API key file. If you want to test at higher throughput during the eval, tell us the target and we’ll coordinate a short capacity bump.

Next steps:
1) I’ll send the eval API key and instructions (today).
2) Neha (copied) can join a 30-min technical call this week to walk through sample payloads and tokenization behavior.
3) You send over the preferred time window and any special compliance questions (SLA/retention/SSO) we should pre-check.

Thanks — excited to get you started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the quick demo — that was helpful. A few quick questions before we kick off the eval: 
1) For the evaluation, is the data we send persisted on Redwood Hosted, and what are the default retention/processing terms?
2) We’ll likely start with ~20 QPS for the test harness but could spike to 50 QPS for short periods. Is that within the temporary bump you mentioned?
3) What’s the plan if we decide we need Dedicated later — how disruptive is migration from Hosted to Dedicated?

Also looping Priya (ops) who will own the security checklist. She may send a SOC2/tech questionnaire.

Best,
Alex
Director of Product, FinTechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & next steps

Hi Alex —

Great questions — answers below.

1) Data retention/processing: For Hosted evaluations we persist request logs for troubleshooting and billing purposes. Default retention for logs during an eval is 30 days; payloads used for model improvement are not used without explicit consent (we can enforce a no-training flag for your account). If Priya has a formal questionnaire, please send it and I’ll route to our security team.

2) Rate limits/capacity bump: 20 QPS steady with spikes to 50 QPS is fine for an evaluation window. I’ve flagged this with our infra team — we can provision an eval increase to 100 QPS burst for short tests if needed. Please confirm your expected burst pattern (duration and frequency) and we’ll provision accordingly.

3) Migration to Dedicated: We support seamless migration paths — same API surface and customer-facing config. Dedicated primarily affects isolation and throughput guarantees (reserved GPUs). In my experience the migration is low-friction: pin the model version, update routing in your integration, and we coordinate a cutover. We can provide a migration checklist if you want to plan that ahead.

Attached: eval-api-key.txt (temporary key + expiry), and redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf (again). Links: https://docs.redwood.com/quickstart | Eval console: https://app.redwood.com/eval/FT-2026-0421

If helpful, Neha can run a 30-min load test with your team tomorrow afternoon to validate latency under 50 QPS.

Cheers,
Marissa

Attachments: eval-api-key.txt, redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T12:36:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & next steps

Hi Alex —

Quick note from the SE side with a sample curl you can drop into your harness to exercise streaming + token behavior:

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <EVAL_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-medium","input":"{your prompt here}","max_tokens":256}'

For load testing we typically recommend starting with 20 QPS sustained and increase in 5–10 QPS steps, measuring p50/p95 latency and token throughput. I’ll bring a simple load script and a sample payload set if we run the session tomorrow.

Also — regarding retention: we can attach a no-training flag on the eval key which prevents data from being used for model training. Ask Priya if that is sufficient and I’ll ensure it’s set.

Happy to jump on a call at 3pm PST tomorrow (I have that slot free) — does that work for you?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Marissa / Neha —

Thanks — that all sounds good. The no-training flag is important for us; Priya will confirm but that should address our main data concerns. 3pm PST tomorrow works for the load test call. We’ll start with 20 QPS and plan a short 5-minute spike to 50 QPS to validate bursts.

I’ll have Priya share the SOC2 questionnaire in a follow-up if needed. Looking forward to the eval key so we can get started.

Best,
Alex
